In a lengthy interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman responded to the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and discussed their vision for a 'tab-less' interface. Watch the video below.

Work features may seamlessly integrate into ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern posted a teaser for her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, "New Things."

Today, Stern released the full interview, covering topics including the new ChatGPT voice mode, OpenAI's hardware plans, the lawsuit against Apple, and the recent Hugging Face breach.

During the interview, Stern mentioned OpenAI's recent decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps together, along with the launch of a new agentic mode for ChatGPT called "Work."

The new interface proved confusing, especially for users who just wanted to keep using ChatGPT and had trouble finding their chats.

OpenAI later updated the app to bring back separate "Work" and "Chat" tabs at the top of the interface, along with a dropdown menu in the sidebar to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app is not as difficult to use as before, it remains slightly more complicated to navigate.

When asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern, admitting the new interface was "a bit messy," while adding that this is "progress" toward the future and that eventually the "Work" tab will disappear, with its features "seamlessly integrating into ChatGPT."

Brockman also said that despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI is seeing the results it expected, with Codex growing from 5 million to 10 million users in just a few days.

When pressed on whether this growth was simply the result of forcing Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman once again admitted it was, but also pointed out that this was partly the point:

The full interview is really interesting and well worth a watch. There's also a very "Joanna Stern" attempt to bring ChatGPT Voice into the conversation, which goes about as "well" as you can imagine.
